- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast slope to avoid premature correction.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40–45), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of gradual upward correction.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., ±0.3), model often overestimates volatility; cap forecast range within ±2–3% of recent 7-day average.  
- If model forecast is consistently > true outcome by 2–4% over 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to align with observed decay.  
- If sentiment shows sudden reversal (e.g., from -0.7 to +0.5), model often fails to adjust; add 1–2 days of upward bias to capture sentiment shift.
